⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Because of the burning rubber smell and the brush stopping, this appliance must be unplugged immediately and should not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it. The most likely cause is that the drive belt snapped under strain (which often produces a burning smell as it frays) or that the electric motor driving the brush failed. While you can safely inspect the floorhead for hair tangles with it unplugged, this does not make it safe to operate; please arrange for professional repair.
